answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable work bond before it may transact, like a jetty that only lets verified boats dock. The bond is released only after peers attest the agent's work is real, and one shared reputation thread ties every action to a single identity, so spawning clones in the tundra of fake accounts gains nothing: each clone must pay its own bond and build its own history, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn back.
